messages:
rachel: hey team — rachel here, just joined yesterday. my first CI runs are mostly green but the publish step fails when pushing to ghcr.io with `401 Unauthorized`. i'm running a mixed workflow: build in Actions, publish from a Buildkite pipeline triggered by the Actions artifact. any obvious things i'm missing?
omar: welcome! :wave: mixed runners can be annoying. which auth are you using in Buildkite? a lot of folks accidentally try to reuse `GITHUB_TOKEN` or an Actions secret that doesn't exist in Buildkite.
rachel: i created a secret called `CI_REG_TOKEN` in Buildkite with my PAT. pipeline step does `echo "$CI_REG_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u rachel --password-stdin` then push. locally the same PAT works. logs show `unauthorized: authentication required` from the push.
neel: two possibilities: 1) PAT lacks `packages:write`, 2) org SSO is blocking the PAT for CI. also check that Buildkite pipeline has access to that secret (pipeline vs team secret scoping).
omar: also confirm the token user has package write access on that repo/org. GHCR permissions can be set at org level for package namespaces.
ci-helper-bot: Buildkite build #12 failed — step "publish" (exit code 1). Logs: failed to copy: unauthorized: authentication required.
rachel: my PAT is new and shows `write:packages` when i created it. what does SSO blocking look like?
neel: if your org enforces SSO, the PAT owner must authorize the token for the org. otherwise requests from external runners will get 401/403. you can check by looking at your org profile or the org settings. if you see a banner about SSO you need to click authorize.
omar: instead of using personal PATs we generally create a machine user like `redwood-ci` and a repo-scoped token. ops rotates it and infra adds it to pipelines as `GHCR_PAT`. that avoids onboarding roadblocks.
rachel: i can't see the org SSO page (403) — i'm not an org admin. who can check authorizations?
neel: tag @ops or ping #eng-infra and we'll handle machine user creation. drop your repo name here and we'll scope the token.
rachel: repo is `examples/onboarding-demo`. i'd prefer machine user.
omar: acknowledged. i'll create `redwood-ci` and add package write permission to examples/onboarding-demo, then add PAT to Buildkite as `GHCR_PAT` (masked pipeline env). once done i'll re-run the build.
gha-bot: GitHub Actions run 412 queued — awaiting artifact from buildkite.
ci-helper-bot: Machine user `redwood-ci` created and PAT added as pipeline secret `GHCR_PAT` (masked). Buildkite app installation approved for repo.
omar: re-triggering build #13 now.
ci-helper-bot: Buildkite build #13 started (branch: onboarding/rachel-first).
ci-helper-bot: Buildkite build #13 succeeded — publish step passed.
rachel:  success! thank you. couple quick follow-ups: 1) where's the minimal doc on secret names and patterns for both Actions and Buildkite? 2) who owns rotating the machine PAT and how do i request rotation for a repo?
neel: docs/dev/ci-auth.md has a short table: GHCR_TOKEN for Actions, GHCR_PAT for Buildkite, machine user recommended. rotations are ops responsibility quarterly; infra will update repo/pipeline secrets on rotation. to request earlier rotation tag #eng-infra + @omar.
rachel: perfect — i'll open a tiny PR to add a line about SSO gotchas. thanks again :tada:
omar: welcome aboard! happy to pair on the rest of the CI config later today.
